title: Introduce debounce + auto-cancel behavior for stacked action button groups
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In multi-action toolbars (stacked/vertical button groups) we see false double-invocations and lingering loading states when users rapidly tap multiple adjacent actions or navigate away mid-request. This causes spurious API calls, confusing simultaneous loading spinners, and occasional visual regressions when themes flip during an in-flight request.

Goal: Define a design spec for a consistent interaction model that applies to stacked/compact action button groups: introduce a short debounce on consecutive taps, visual affordances for grouped pending state, and an auto-cancel flow that gracefully reverts UI when the user navigates or when another higher-priority action supersedes the previous one. Ensure the behavior works across themes, high-contrast, reduced-motion, and with assistive tech.

Scope: Design tokens to update (focus/outline, group spacing, spinner placement), interaction patterns (debounce window, cancellation affordance), ARIA/keyboard flow, and visual regression test criteria. This ticket is focused on the design spec + prototype and handoff assets; ENG tickets will implement runtime enforcement and telemetry hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec describes debounce interval (default 250ms) and when it may be overridden per product context
Grouped pending state: visual treatment for 'stacked' groups where only the active action shows spinner while siblings show subtle dim/blocked state
Auto-cancel cases enumerated: navigation away, explicit cancel via escape/primary keyboard shortcut, and superseding action taken in same group
Accessibility: keyboard focus and activation still triggers one action; aria-live region announces action start/complete; screen reader flow tested in VoiceOver and NVDA
Theme parity verified: light/dark/high-contrast and dynamic theme swaps during pending state do not produce layout shifts or spinner color regressions
Prototype in Figma linked and interactive keyboard/click flows documented
Design handoff includes tokens changes, motion reduction variant, and QA checklist for engineering and visual-regression owners
engineering_notes: Coordinate with ENG runtime team to expose a per-group debounce config and an opt-in auto-cancel callback. Runtime should expose telemetry hooks: action_id, cancelled_by, duration_ms, and theme_at_dispatch. Proposed ENG work: ENG-31245 (group-interaction-runtime) and ENG-31256 (telemetry-hooks). If implementation needs to change debounce to 200ms for perf reasons, update design token and document rationale.
qa_tests: Rapid tap sequence on stacked group should only fire a single request within debounce window

Trigger action, then immediately navigate to a different route; UI should surface cancel affordance and firing request should be cancelled if supported by client code - otherwise UI must clear pending state after safe timeout
With reduced-motion preference enabled, spinner should be replaced by a non-animated pending badge
Switch theme during pending state and verify no layout shift and spinner color remains accessible
Screen reader: activate first action in group then quickly attempt second - verify single action announced and no duplicate announcements
review_feedback: PM (Evan Li): Prefer conservative defaults — start with 250ms debounce. Provide clear opt-out for critical actions.
Engineering (Rohit Mehra): Ensure debounce logic lives in runtime layer not just component; need a fallback for network-unreliable clients.
Accessibility (Lydia Cruz): Add explicit aria-atomic region for pending state updates; recommend announcing 'Action started' and 'Action cancelled' messages for clarity.
Design (Maya Thompson): Use existing spinner token but add 'stacked-pending' color token so we can adjust contrast without touching global spinner.
decisions: Default debounce window: 250ms (can be overridden by prop/context)
Stacked groups show single active spinner; siblings render a subtle blocked overlay token (token: button.group-blocked-overlay)
Auto-cancel is a visual-first pattern: UI can clear pending state immediately but runtime cancellation requires explicit opt-in and capability on the consumer; spec documents both flows
Reduced-motion uses non-animated badge with same semantic meaning as spinner
ARIA: use aria-live polite for start/completion; ensure focus is preserved on action trigger
tasks: Create ENG tickets for runtime debounce + telemetry (blocker) (Maya)
Design token PR: introduce button.group-blocked-overlay & button.stack-spinner-color (Aisha)
Accessibility testing session with Assistive Tech team (Lydia)
